depth_to_points — 3D transform op

• Data kinds: depth → points

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.depth_to_points(depth, fx, fy, cx, cy, stride=1) (to call the implementation directly, import match3d; match3d.depth_to_points(depth, fx, fy, cx, cy, stride=1); from the registry, ops3d.get("depth_to_points"))

Usage

Depth map (2.5-D) → point cloud (pinhole back-projection). It connects the depth row to every method.

From the depth z of pixel (row v, column u), X = (u − cx)·z/fx, Y = (v − cy)·z/fy, Z = z are formed. Returns (N,3) float64; the columns are camera coordinates (X, Y, Z) (same unit as the depth). Pixels with z of 0 or less are discarded, so N is at most the number of pixels (convention: invalid depth is represented by 0).

• fx, fy, cx, cy: focal length and principal point in pixels. Same convention as K in project_points.

• stride: rows and columns are both thinned to every stride-th pixel. u, v are the post-thinning index multiplied by stride,

i.e. computed as pixel coordinates of the original image, so thinning does not change the geometry.

• No input validation (if not 2-D, indexing fails). NaN depths are discarded because z > 0 is false.

• Points are ordered row-major, but the row/column information is not kept. To keep the grid structure, use

depth_to_organized_points.

Downstream: points_to_voxel / estimate_point_normals / icp_point2plane. Inverse mapping: project_points; TSDF conversion: tsdf_from_depth.
